paragraphs: In the club hour, Leo showed a new board game to Lily and May. He made it from a big green card and some colored paper. He drew small waves and many fish on it with a blue pen. At the end of the board, there was a big whale. The name of the game was Deep Sea Trip. He wrote the rules on a small card, and Lily read them. Lily and May wanted to play, so they sat at the table.
"How to start. Two to four players can play. Each player needs a piece of a different color. Put your piece on Start. Throw the dice. The player with the biggest number goes first.

How to move. Throw the dice, and move your piece. Move the same number of squares as the dice. Then the next player throws the dice. Never move without throwing the dice. On a red square, act like a sea animal. The other players guess the animal. If you land on a blue square, you are in the deep sea. Go back two squares. On a yellow square, lie on the floor like a fish and count to five.
How to win. The first player to get to the Big Whale wins. A friend can join the game at any time. Be kind, and have fun."

Leo put three pieces on the first square. Each child threw the dice, and Lily got a six. Six was the biggest number, so she went first. She moved six squares and stopped on a red square. Lily acted like a shark, and May guessed the animal at once. Then May threw a four. She stopped on a blue square, and she went back two squares. May laughed. "It is wonderful!" said May. "Can we play again next Thursday?" asked Lily. Leo smiled and said, "Yes, and Teacher Kim can join us."
